extracted.intended_audience: NIH R21 applicants, peer reviewers, and grants staff (investigators preparing or responding to NIH peer review)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and review criteria used by an NIH study section to evaluate an R21 grant application, including criterion-level scores, overall impact, human subjects and compliance determinations, and budget recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates whether the project addresses an important problem and the potential to alter prevailing paradigms (e.g., 'The research in this application should lead to a paradigm shift ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list strengths and weaknesses specific to significance (e.g., public health importance, potential to identify high-risk newborns). Example scoring on this application: Significance: 1-2 (lower numbers indicate higher merit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the qualifications, productivity, and suitability of the PI and key personnel for the proposed work (e.g., 'The PI has a long and highly accomplished record ... exceptionally well-suited for these studies').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers comment on strengths/weaknesses of the investigative team, relevant expertise, and collaborations. Example scoring on this application: Investigator(s): 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates novelty of concepts, approaches, methods, or interventions (e.g., applying the concept of 'layering' to human neonatal immunity; developing transcriptional signatures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers identify innovative aspects and note any concerns. Example scoring on this application: Innovation: 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses the overall strategy, methodology, analyses, and feasibility (e.g., clear presentation of experimental approach, data analysis plan, powered study design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers enumerate approach strengths (preliminary data, clear methods, collaborators) and weaknesses (feasibility concerns such as blood volume limits, marker identification). Example scoring on this application: Approach: 1-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges institutional support, resources, and research environment (e.g., 'The environment at UCSF and the associated clinical sites is essentially perfect').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note whether environment materially contributes to likelihood of success; score example: Environment: 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Impact-Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary judgment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field; presented as an Impact/Priority Score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact/priority scores are numeric (1-9 per reviewer), averaged across voting reviewers and multiplied by 10 to yield the final score. The summary statement provides reviewers' narrative supporting the overall impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion Scores Submission & Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural guidance on scoring: 'The criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by the individual reviewers assigned to an application...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are submitted prior to the review meeting, are not discussed specifically at the meeting, and are not calculated into the overall impact score (overall impact is derived from reviewers' overall scores averaged and multiplied by 10). See NIH peer review process link for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of human subjects protections and risk (e.g., 'Acceptable Risks and/or Adequate Protections'; 'No concerns').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers state whether protections are acceptable and list any concerns. The summary may include a short resume statement such as 'PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS (Resume): ACCEPTABLE.' Also shows Human Subjects involvement classification (e.g., '30-Human subjects involved - Certified, no SRG concerns').

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that a Data and Safety Monitoring Plan is required when applicable: 'Data and Safety Monitoring Plan (Applicable for Clinical Trials Only)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, reviewers comment on the adequacy of the monitoring plan; if not applicable, indicate so. No detailed plan text provided in this example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of inclusion plans using NIH coding (e.g., 'G1A - Both Genders, Acceptable', 'M1A - Minority and Non-minority, Acceptable', 'C1A – Children Included, Acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers (and the summary resume) indicate acceptability of inclusion plans; codes and short judgments (Acceptable/Not Acceptable) are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination regarding use of vertebrate animals (e.g., 'Not Applicable (No Vertebrate Animals)') and any concerns if used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If animals are involved, reviewers assess appropriateness and protections; if not applicable, state so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of biohazard concerns (e.g., 'Biohazards: Acceptable'; 'Human blood products, acceptable').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note whether biohazard protections are adequate and list concerns if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of the study's relevance to public health (e.g., potential to identify newborns at risk and tailor immunization strategies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are expected to provide a concise public health relevance paragraph; reviewers comment on its importance and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths and Weaknesses Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers present per-criterion bulleted 'Strengths' and 'Weaknesses' to justify scores (seen repeatedly under Significance, Innovation, Approach, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each criterion's narrative should include explicit strengths and weaknesses; strengths often cite preliminary data, environment, collaborators, and feasibility, while weaknesses highlight feasibility gaps, missing details, or risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support / Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee provides budget recommendation and notes administrative handling (e.g., 'Recommend as Requested'; 'ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET NOTE: The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations... costs will be calculated by Institute grants management staff based on the recommendations outlined below').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review can recommend funding as requested or with changes; final funding amounts are determined by grants management in accordance with committee recommendations and Institute policies.
